clue.text: Work the land in infamous prison

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, so the farming word goes within the vile word

parts.note: base means vile or dishonourable, so infamous
to till is to plough and cultivate soil

explanation.surface: Farm labour carried out inside a notorious jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infamous prison' looks like one phrase for the whole definition, but 'infamous' is wordplay meaning vile, and only 'prison' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris fortress stormed in 1789 served as a state jail.

clue.text: Reproach worker eating vermin

indicators.note: the insect word swallows the vermin word

parts.note: a worker bee
a rat is vermin

explanation.surface: A labourer chewing on a rodent gets a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone sharply is to rebuke them.

clue.text: Password for avuncular American entering bishopric

indicators.note: the American goes into the bishop's diocese word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
Uncle Sam personifies the USA, avuncular meaning uncle-like

explanation.surface: A friendly American gives the password to get into a diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open sesame' is the magic password from Ali Baba.
explanation.definitionFit: The magic word that opens the robbers' cave in the Arabian Nights tale.

clue.text: One does not start a fire

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is not lighting a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a fireplace or hearth fire.

clue.text: Pick fish up from this direction

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: draw means pick, as when drawing lots
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler pulls a fish up from this side.
explanation.definitionFit: The side facing away from the wind, as a nautical heading.

clue.text: Books included in substantial charge

indicators.note: the books abbreviation is placed within the word for substantial

parts.note: substantial means actual, existing, so real
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A hefty fee that comes with some books thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hire payment is the fee charged for using something.

clue.text: Rose's inelegant disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Rose has a clumsy temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name; it is the flower. 'disposition' rearranges INELEGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet briar, a wild species of the flower.

clue.text: Reptile quietly hiding in the landscape

indicators.note: the soft letter is concealed within the landscape word

parts.note: terrain is landscape
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A reptile lurks silently in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle.

clue.text: Horror of a fine appearing in report

indicators.note: the pieces show up inside the record word

parts.note: a log is a written record or report
fine means thin, as fine thread

explanation.surface: Dread of being fined, shown up in an official report.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense hatred or disgust is a feeling of revulsion.

clue.text: Soldier gestured for patient

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier
signed means made a sign or gesture

explanation.surface: A soldier waved a signal for someone in his care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like a noun for someone in hospital; here it is the adjective meaning uncomplaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accepting their lot without complaint is calm and long-suffering.

clue.text: Girl is out of the ordinary

definitions.meaning: the Ordinary of the Mass is its fixed sung text, and this hymn of praise comes from it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the girl is unusual; the second reading takes 'the ordinary' as the Ordinary of the Mass, from which this hymn comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and also the Latin hymn of praise that forms part of the unchanging sections of the Mass.

clue.text: Support old construction toy

parts.note: a leg supports a table

explanation.surface: An old prop for a building toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of interlocking plastic bricks for children.

clue.text: Paddy consumed mild

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper (British informal)
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: An Irishman ate his food quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like a name (an Irishman); in British slang a paddy is a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate weather or behaviour is gentle and free of extremes.

clue.text: Smart hotel in Wales

parts.note: smart means tidy, so neat
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A stylish hotel somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: NEATH is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A town near Swansea in the south of the principality.

clue.text: Conspicuous fellow embraces sovereign

indicators.note: the word for fellow wraps around the coin letter

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or fellow
a sovereign is a gold one-pound coin, and L stands for pound

explanation.surface: A showy man hugging a king.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth a pound, abbreviated L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking stands out clearly to the eye.

clue.text: Looking up those people in winning design

indicators.note: the people word goes inside the other pair

parts.note: on means successful, as in being on form
an end is an aim or design
them means those people

explanation.surface: People looking at a winning design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up' seems literal; it means improving.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering or improving, as a patient or situation gets better.

clue.text: View duck's wing

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: A look at the wing of a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A considered belief is someone's personal take on a matter.

clue.text: Winger looking to bring in money

indicators.note: the gazing word takes the money letter inside

parts.note: staring means looking hard
L stands for pound, money

explanation.surface: A wing player hoping to earn some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' sounds like a footballer; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A common songbird is a creature with wings.

clue.text: Man catching a perch is tall and thin

definitions.note: adjectival phrase for a noun describing a lanky person

indicators.note: the name grabs the letter a inside it

parts.note: Ben is a man's name
a pole or perch is an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A man who catches a fish is lanky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like a fish; it is a measure of length equal to a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanky person is likened to the stick that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Dine with rector in the hall

indicators.note: the eating word and the rector letter go inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Having dinner with the vicar in the great hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a hall where plays are staged.

clue.text: Flair embodied by Michaelangelo

indicators.note: the letters sit within the painter's name

explanation.surface: The painter's talent was clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash and stylish vigour.

clue.text: Good shelter produces good spirits

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A decent refuge makes people cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriment is a state of cheerful high spirits.

clue.text: Old maid, for example, left an oriental orchestra

parts.note: old maid is a card game
L is left

explanation.surface: An elderly spinster left an Eastern band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old maid' is a children's card game.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indonesian ensemble of gongs and metallophones.

clue.text: A king without character makes amends

definitions.note: verb phrase for a noun meaning one who does so

indicators.note: without means outside, so the A and the king letter surround the character word

parts.note: R is rex, king
tone means character or quality

explanation.surface: A characterless king seeks to make up for it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who expiates wrongdoing is a person who pays penance.

clue.text: French person in British school

parts.note: BR is British
Eton is an English public school

explanation.surface: A French pupil at a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Brittany in north-west France.

clue.text: Anger having knight in the province

indicators.note: the word for anger has the knight letter inside it

parts.note: anger means rage
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Fury at a knight in the provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: A scope or sphere of activity is someone's area or domain.

clue.text: Two masters introduced to change their own college

indicators.note: the two degree abbreviations are put inside the word for change

parts.note: change means alter
MA, Master of Arts, taken twice
MA, Master of Arts, taken twice

explanation.surface: Two masters' degree holders arrive to reform their old college.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for nourishing mother, the usual term for the school or university someone attended.

clue.text: Defaces hospital in Slough

parts.note: mars means spoils or defaces
H is hospital

explanation.surface: Vandals damage a hospital in Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the English town; it means a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a boggy wetland.

clue.text: Iran seizes quantity of chemical similar to another

indicators.note: the Iran code grips the quantity word between its letters

parts.note: IR is the international code for Iran
some means an amount or quantity

explanation.surface: Iran confiscates a stock of a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound with the same formula as another but its atoms arranged differently.

clue.text: Arranged recital including new instrument

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters are reordered, as music is arranged

explanation.surface: A recital, arranged for performance, featuring a new instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges RECITAL with N for new.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Eager journalist in depressing environment

indicators.note: the gloomy word forms the surroundings of the journalist

parts.note: grey means dull and gloomy, so depressing
ED, an editor, stands for a journalist

explanation.surface: A keen reporter in a gloomy office.
explanation.definitionFit: Being avid for something means wanting it badly.

clue.text: Fugitive is no hunter, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A runaway who is unfortunately no hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person escaping capture is fleeing from pursuit.
